A study on prospects of organic   farming in Haryana 
P.I.: 
Dr.   B.S.Ghanghas
Co-PI:   
Dr. P.K. Chahal 

Organic farming was perceived   highly prospective by 60.00 percent of farmers especially on aspects such as   environment friendly, improves soil health, products are safe, healthy and   nutritious, reduce dependence on external inputs for farming, enhances the   employment opportunities, demand of organic products is increasing due to   high health and nutrition awareness among people, helps in conserving natural   resources & biodiversity as well organic produce fetches high price   resulting in higher income. The major constraints faced by organic farmers   were viz.  no special  incentive or remunerative price policy by   the government  for organic produce,   lack of agencies to purchase organic products, , lack of marketing   intelligence for organic produce, lack of mobilization of organic farmers in   groups/community based organizations or social organization for promotion of   organic farming.
A study on present status of  inland fishery adoption in Haryana
P.I.: 
Dr.   B.S.Ghanghas
Co-PI:   
Dr. P.K. Chahal 

The overall adoption for fish   farming technology was found low since 56.00 per cent of respondent farmers   belonged to this category. It was mainly due to less or no adoption of   practices viz. control of aquatic weeds, ploughing of pond, disease control measures   and application of recommended manures and fertilizers. Lack of knowledge of   field functionaries for post harvest management practices, lack of knowledge   of modern storage structures, non availability of fish feed & seed at   proper time in villages, lack of remunerative fish MSP policy, wide price   fluctuations, high price of fish seed and no cold storages at villages were   major constraints faced by fish farmers of Haryana.
 Enhancing Farm Productivity and   Profitability by Technological Interventions through Farmers’ Participatory   Approach in Hisar District Farmer   FIRST Programme

P.I.: 
Dr.   R.S.Hudda
Co-PI:   
Dr. P.K. Chahal 

Impact of FFP:
 A positive impact of Farmer FIRST Programme was   observed among the farmers of both the selected villages i.e. Bure and   Dubetta.  The farmers are socially   motivated towards diversification as they observed profit and social   recognition. Moreover, the farmers are getting more income due to   demonstrations under FFP that ultimately upscaled their social status and make   their livelihood secure. Fellow farmers of selected villages and nearby   villages also got influenced by the farmers of FFP, CCSHAU, Hisar.
Constraints: 
Unavailability of quality seed in time. 
Moisture stress at critical stages of crop growth   which results in lesser yield. 
Bed planting technology in wheat benefits the   farmers, but its successful adoption depends on a favorable confluence of   technical, economic and institutional factors. 
Lack of access to good physical, economic/financial,   social infrastructure such as marketing and processing facilities, godowns,   etc.
Need of advanced capacity building of farmers on   post harvest and value addition. 
Way Forward:
Needed   horizontal extension of villages under Farmer FIRST Programme.
Water requirement was a major   problem faced by farmers during crop growing period, so water harvesting   structures should be developed.
Provision   of quality seeds and nutrients based   on soil health of each field.
Needed large scale investment in warehousing and cold   chains  to prevent  post harvest crop losses.
Project   villages may be developed as Agro-eco-tourism   spots in Public Private   Partnership (PPP) mode.
 A study on the present status of custom   hiring centers for farm mechanization in Haryana
P.I.: 
Dr.   B.S.Ghanghas
Co-PI:   
Dr. P.K. Chahal 

A vast majority of farmers   (84.45%) utilized services of CHCs purely for hiring machinery for farm   operations followed by running own centres and pooling of machinery i.e.   11.11 & 4.44 percent respectively. High initial costs, no rate fixation   by village committees and insufficient no. of machinery or implements at peak   seasons were very serious constraints related to inputs of CHCs for their   promotion.  Similarly, delayed operations   through false promises to keep intact the customer, no pooling of machinery,   farm implements or driver services etc, high hiring charges especially at   aberrant weather conditions at maturity of crops and poor quality of service   at peak seasons were very serious constraints faced by farmers in utilization   of CHC services. Whereas,  middle man   malpractices, no use of ICTs for availability updates by owners  and no labour offer for certain ancillary   operations were found least serious ornot so serious constraints by farmers for effective and efficient   utilization of services
Communication pattern of field   functionaries of Horticulture Department in Haryana.
P.I.: 
Dr.   B.S.Ghanghas
Co-PI:   
Dr. P.K. Chahal 

Most   popular global media namely social media like Whats App and You Tube  was most frequently used information source   with top ranking by field functionaries among communication linkages for   acquisition of production and protection technologies of horticultural crops   followed by package of practices for horticultural crops, trainings,   internet, staff meetings, subject matter specialist of department, leaflets,   pamphlets, folders and technical bulletins, krishi melas, scientist   (CCSHAU/MPU/ICAR/Training institute) & websites of agricultural   universities/ICAR/ research institutes/centres of excellence of horticultural   crops. The field functionaries used pragmatic approach for information   processing, preservation and transformation viz. suitability, economic   advantage and feasibility for processing the information while, careful study   of useful information and translation into local dialect respectively for   preservation and transformation were always used by them. Field visits   followed by answering clients' questions, distribution of information   materials, personal telephone calls, trainings, farmers meetings and office   calls were the regularly used methods by functionaries for transfer of   production and protection technologies of horticultural crops to farmers   while they rarely used or not used mass media viz. television talks, radio   talks followed by minikit trials virtual trainings/e-chaupals on face book or   YouTube and crop competitions. The probable reason for low use of these might   be due to newly appointed staff with no experience along with higher   engagements in office work. So department should make sincere efforts in   capacity building on conducting farm trials, crop competitions for greater   motivation and higher adoption of innovative technologies along with delivery   of mass media talks for enhancing their outreach & effective and   efficient contingent services by functionaries.

Zero   tillage was most adopted in-situ paddy residue management practice by 60.00   percent of farmers while M B plough and chemical/biological decomposition   were least adopted or not adopted by farmers. Whereas, partial burning was   still used by 52.50 per cent of farmers for off-situ management of residues   followed by sale through open auction at farm itself and no adoption of   compost making and mushroom production was found. Increased use of combine   harvester for crops leading to long stubbles/high biomass load in the field,   close window of sowing in wheat-paddy system and crop residues interfere with   tillage operation were very serious technical constraints faced by all   farmers followed by no assured procurement/ purchase by government   organizations/institutions/industries, Basmati paddy straw’s preferred   purchase by unorganized private partiesas very serious marketing constraints while, incorporation as well   bailing enhance the cost of cultivation due to high power and costly   machinery  & high cost incurred in   straw removing & transportation of voluminous mass from the field were   very serious financial constraints encountered  along withcompost making being time consuming as well as labour intensive along   with high labour wages as management constraints , besides paddy residue has   low local economic domestic use,non  availability of suitable   straw management technologies followed by insufficient energy industry/ power   plants, paper and board industries in the region for consumption of paddy   straw were very serious constraints faced by large number of farmers in   effective and efficient management of paddy straw
